title: The walk
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: The dog wants out. The strip discovers the beach.

panels.composition: Morning. BARNABY at the bedroom door, leash in mouth. There is no leash. He has a sock. WOOD at the table.

characters.pose: at the door with a sock in his mouth

image.prompt: a scruffy dog standing at a bedroom door holding a sock in its mouth, looking at a young man at a drawing table

panels.composition: Barnaby, still at the door. The sock. Wood's pen. A standoff.

image.prompt: a standoff between a dog holding a sock at a door and a young man at a drawing table with his pen hovering

panels.composition: The beach. Sideways rain. Barnaby ahead, barking at a wave. Wood behind, coat over his head.

image.prompt: a wide beach in sideways rain, a low-slung dog barking at a breaking wave, a young man behind with his coat pulled over his head, brush-pen black and white

panels.composition: Wood stopped, coat off his head, looking at the light through the spruce grove at the beach's edge. Barnaby dragging him toward it by the sock.

image.prompt: a young man stopped on a beach looking at light breaking through a spruce grove while a small dog tugs him forward by a sock, no words
image.notes: The first Arthur-and-Barnaby walk: the strip drops the jokes and lets the landscape in.

art.line: brush-pen now — the weekday deadline teaches the hand to commit; still xeroxed, still black and white
art.paper: the college paper's newsprint; the digest's quarter-letter xerox

notes: The first walk. The template for fifteen years of them.
